deck_name: Golden Dawn Tarot — Book T with Rider-Waite-Smith Imagery

major-00-the-fool.name: 0 — The Fool
major-00-the-fool.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A youth in a motley coat stands at the edge of a cliff, his face turned toward the sun. A white dog leaps at his heels. He carries a white rose in one hand and a staff with a pack over his shoulder. Below the cliff, mountains drop away. He steps forward without looking down.

major-01-the-magician.name: 1 — The Magician
major-01-the-magician.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A red-robed figure stands at a table bearing a cup, a wand, a sword, and a pentacle — the four suit emblems. His right hand raises a wand toward the sky; his left points downward. Above his head a lemniscate (figure-eight loop) floats. Roses and lilies border the scene.

major-02-the-high-priestess.name: 2 — The High Priestess
major-02-the-high-priestess.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A robed woman sits between two pillars — one black (B) and one white (J). She holds a scroll partially concealed beneath her robe. A crescent moon rests at her feet. Behind her, a veil decorated with pomegranates separates the visible world from the hidden.

major-03-the-empress.name: 3 — The Empress
major-03-the-empress.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A crowned woman sits on a cushioned throne in a lush field. She wears a robe patterned with pomegranates and holds a scepter. At her feet, a wheat field grows. A waterfall flows in the background. A shield bearing the symbol of Venus leans beside her.

major-04-the-emperor.name: 4 — The Emperor
major-04-the-emperor.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

An armored man sits on a stone throne decorated with ram-head carvings. He holds a scepter in the shape of the ankh in his right hand and an orb in his left. Behind him, barren red mountains rise under an orange sky. He wears a red robe and a golden crown.

major-05-the-hierophant.name: 5 — The Hierophant
major-05-the-hierophant.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A robed figure in a triple crown sits enthroned between two pillars. He raises his right hand in a gesture of blessing with two fingers extended. Two tonsured acolytes kneel before him. A set of crossed keys lies at his feet.

major-06-the-lovers.name: 6 — The Lovers
major-06-the-lovers.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man and a woman stand naked in a garden. Behind the woman is the Tree of Knowledge with a serpent coiled around it. Behind the man is a tree bearing twelve flames. An angel with spread wings and a solar nimbus hovers above, arms extended in blessing.

major-07-the-chariot.name: 7 — The Chariot
major-07-the-chariot.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A crowned warrior stands within a canopied chariot drawn by two sphinxes — one black, one white. He holds a wand and wears a breastplate with crescent moons on the shoulders. Stars decorate the canopy above. The sphinxes face in different directions but the chariot moves forward.

major-08-strength.name: 8 — Strength
major-08-strength.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A woman in a white dress adorned with flowers closes the jaws of a lion with her bare hands. Above her head floats a lemniscate. The lion lowers its head compliantly. Mountain peaks rise in the blue background. Her posture is calm and effortless.

major-09-the-hermit.name: 9 — The Hermit
major-09-the-hermit.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

An old man in a gray robe stands on a mountain peak. He holds a lit lantern aloft in his right hand; inside the lantern a six-pointed star glows. His left hand grips a tall staff. He looks downward, his long white beard falling across his chest.

major-10-wheel-of-fortune.name: 10 — Wheel of Fortune
major-10-wheel-of-fortune.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A large wheel turns in the sky, inscribed with letters. A sphinx sits atop the wheel holding a sword. A serpent descends the left side; a jackal-headed figure rises on the right. Four winged creatures occupy the corners — angel, eagle, lion, and bull — each reading from a book.

major-11-justice.name: 11 — Justice
major-11-justice.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A crowned woman sits between two pillars on a throne. She holds an upright double-edged sword in her right hand and a set of scales in her left. Her expression is impassive. A purple veil hangs behind her between the pillars.

major-12-the-hanged-man.name: 12 — The Hanged Man
major-12-the-hanged-man.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man hangs upside-down from a T-shaped wooden cross, suspended by his right foot. His left leg is bent behind the right, forming a cross with his legs. His hands are behind his back and his expression is calm. A halo of light surrounds his head.

major-13-death.name: 13 — Death
major-13-death.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A skeleton in black armor rides a white horse across a field. Under the horse lie a fallen king, a child, and a woman who has fainted. A bishop in white robes faces the skeleton with hands raised. In the background, two towers frame a setting sun. The skeleton carries a black banner with a white rose.

major-14-temperance.name: 14 — Temperance
major-14-temperance.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A winged androgynous figure stands with one foot on land and one in water. The figure pours water between two cups in a continuous stream that defies gravity. On the figure's chest is a triangle within a square. Irises bloom at the water's edge. A solar crown appears in the sky on a path leading into the distance.

major-15-the-devil.name: 15 — The Devil
major-15-the-devil.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A horned, bat-winged figure stands on a pedestal. Chained to the pedestal below are a man and a woman, both horned and with tails. The Devil's right hand is raised in an inverted blessing; his left holds a downward-pointing torch. An inverted pentagram is inscribed on the Devil's forehead.

major-16-the-tower.name: 16 — The Tower
major-16-the-tower.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A stone tower is struck by a lightning bolt, knocking a crown from its top. Flames burst from two windows and from the crown. Two figures fall headfirst from the tower, one wearing a crown. Twenty-two falling sparks or yods surround the tower as it collapses.

major-17-the-star.name: 17 — The Star
major-17-the-star.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A naked woman kneels at the edge of a pool. She pours water from two jugs — one onto the land, one into the pool. Eight stars fill the sky: one large eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones. A bird perches in a tree at the right. The woman's expression is serene.

major-18-the-moon.name: 18 — The Moon
major-18-the-moon.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A full moon with a face inside a crescent shines over a pool. A crayfish or lobster emerges from the water. A wolf and a dog face each other, both howling at the moon. Two towers frame the scene on either side. A path between the towers winds into the distant mountains.

major-19-the-sun.name: 19 — The Sun
major-19-the-sun.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A radiant sun with a face shines over a stone wall from which sunflowers grow. A naked child rides a white horse in the foreground, arms outstretched, a large red banner or feather in their hand. Twenty-one rays radiate from the sun alternating between straight and wavy.

major-20-judgement.name: 20 — Judgement
major-20-judgement.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

An angel with wings blows a trumpet from which a banner hangs. Below, naked figures rise from gray coffins opening in the sea. The figures — a man, a woman, and a child — raise their arms upward. Mountains of ice form the background.

major-21-the-world.name: 21 — The World
major-21-the-world.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A naked figure draped in a purple cloth dances inside an oval wreath. The figure holds two wands, one in each hand. In the four corners appear the same four living creatures as the Wheel of Fortune — angel, eagle, lion, and bull. The wreath is bound at top and bottom with a red ribbon.

wands-ace.name: Ace of Wands
wands-ace.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A hand emerges from a cloud holding a sprouting wooden club or wand. Small leaves bud from the branch. A castle and landscape appear in the background. The wand points upward.

wands-02.name: Two of Wands
wands-02.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man in a red robe stands on a castle battlement, looking out over sea and land. He holds a globe in his right hand and a wand in his left. A second wand is fixed beside him in the wall. Roses and lilies decorate the parapet.

wands-03.name: Three of Wands
wands-03.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A figure stands with their back to the viewer on a cliff edge, looking out over water where three ships sail. Three wands are planted in the ground around them. The figure holds one of them lightly with their right hand.

wands-04.name: Four of Wands
wands-04.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Four wands are planted in the ground, their tops draped with a garland of flowers and fruits. Beyond them, two women celebrate holding bouquets. In the background, the towers and walls of a city are visible.

wands-05.name: Five of Wands
wands-05.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Five young men engage in a scuffle or mock battle, each brandishing a wand. Their poses are energetic and overlapping. The scene is on a flat plain with no background detail beyond grass.

wands-06.name: Six of Wands
wands-06.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man on horseback carries a wand aloft with a laurel wreath attached to it. Five other figures march beside and below him, each carrying a wand. He appears to be returning in triumph.

wands-07.name: Seven of Wands
wands-07.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man stands on elevated ground, brandishing a wand at six wands thrust upward toward him from below. His expression is determined. He holds the high ground, defending his position.

wands-08.name: Eight of Wands
wands-08.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Eight wands fly through the air in parallel, tilting slightly downward as if in motion toward their target. The sky is clear. A landscape with a river appears below. There are no human figures.

wands-09.name: Nine of Wands
wands-09.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A bandaged man leans on a wand as if injured or weary. Behind him, eight wands stand in a row like a fence. His expression is guarded but resolute, as if prepared for one more challenge.

wands-10.name: Ten of Wands
wands-10.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A figure bends under the burden of ten wands, all carried together in both arms, obscuring his face. He walks toward a town visible in the background. His posture expresses effort and encumbrance.

wands-knight.name: Knight of Wands
wands-knight.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A knight in red armor charges forward on a leaping horse. He holds a wand at an angle and his scarf streams behind him. The landscape is arid with low hills. The horse rears slightly, full of energy.

wands-queen.name: Queen of Wands
wands-queen.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A queen sits on a golden throne decorated with lion heads and sunflowers. She holds a tall wand in her right hand and a sunflower in her left. A black cat sits at her feet. Sunflowers bloom behind her and lions adorn the throne.

wands-king.name: King of Wands
wands-king.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A king sits on a throne decorated with lion and salamander motifs. He holds a long wand and wears a robe with salamander emblems. He looks to one side with a forthright expression. A small salamander appears near his feet.

wands-page.name: Page of Wands
wands-page.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man in a tunic and tall feathered hat stands on a flat plain, holding a tall wand. He looks at the wand intently. Pyramids or mountains appear in the desert background. He stands alone, contemplating.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A hand emerges from a cloud holding a large golden cup or chalice. Five streams of water pour from the cup into a pool below. A dove descends bearing a wafer inscribed with a cross. Water lilies float below.

cups-02.name: Two of Cups
cups-02.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man and woman face each other, each holding a cup and toasting. Above them, a caduceus with a winged lion floats. Both figures are dressed elaborately, suggesting a betrothal or union.

cups-03.name: Three of Cups
cups-03.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Three women lift their cups in a celebratory toast, dancing in a circle. Flowers and fruit surround them, with a plentiful harvest visible underfoot.

cups-04.name: Four of Cups
cups-04.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man sits cross-legged beneath a tree, arms folded, contemplating three cups on the grass before him. A fourth cup is offered by a hand from a cloud, but he does not look at it.

cups-05.name: Five of Cups
cups-05.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A cloaked figure faces three spilled cups on the ground, their contents flowing away. Behind the figure, two cups remain upright. A bridge and castle appear in the background.

cups-06.name: Six of Cups
cups-06.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young boy hands a cup filled with white flowers to a young girl in a garden. Five more cups similarly planted with flowers stand around them. A figure in a cloak walks away in the background.

cups-07.name: Seven of Cups
cups-07.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A silhouetted figure reaches toward seven cups floating in a cloud, each containing a different vision: a castle, gems, a wreath, a dragon, a human face, a veiled figure, and a serpent.

cups-08.name: Eight of Cups
cups-08.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A figure in a red cloak walks away through a mountainous night landscape, leaving behind eight upright cups arranged in a row. The moon is visible in the upper sky. The cups stand abandoned.

cups-09.name: Nine of Cups
cups-09.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A satisfied man sits with arms folded before a curved arrangement of nine golden cups on a shelf behind him. His posture suggests contentment and material well-being.

cups-10.name: Ten of Cups
cups-10.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A couple stands arm in arm beneath a rainbow arc of ten cups. Two children dance nearby. A house and green hills form a peaceful background. The scene evokes domestic fulfillment.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A knight in armor rides slowly on a calm gray horse across flat ground near water. He holds a cup forward in his right hand and looks into it. His helmet sports large wings. His movement is deliberate and unhurried.

cups-queen.name: Queen of Cups
cups-queen.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A queen sits on a throne at the edge of the sea. She gazes into an elaborate covered cup, as if reading it. Her throne is decorated with fish and mermaids. She is contemplative and absorbed.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A king sits on a throne floating amid rough waters. He holds a cup in one hand and a scepter in the other. A fish leaps from the sea behind him. Despite the tumult of the water, he sits in command.

cups-page.name: Page of Cups
cups-page.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man in a flower-patterned tunic stands at the sea's edge, looking at a fish that has emerged from the cup he holds. The fish appears to speak to him. He holds the cup gingerly, surprised.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A hand emerges from a cloud holding an upright sword. A golden crown sits on the tip of the blade, hung with a wreath. Mountains and a valley appear below. The crown suggests victory or judgment.

swords-02.name: Two of Swords
swords-02.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A blindfolded woman sits before the sea, holding two crossed swords horizontally across her chest. Behind her the water is calm and a crescent moon is reflected in it. Her posture is still, balanced, and defended.

swords-03.name: Three of Swords
swords-03.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Three swords pierce a red heart, which floats against a gray sky with rain falling. There are no figures — only the heart and the swords.

swords-04.name: Four of Swords
swords-04.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A knight lies in effigy on a stone tomb, hands clasped in prayer. Three swords hang on the wall above him; a fourth lies along his side. A stained-glass window shows a figure kneeling before another.

swords-05.name: Five of Swords
swords-05.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A smirking man collects three swords while two defeated figures walk away in the distance, their swords left on the ground. The sky is cloudy and turbulent. The victor seems satisfied; the losers are dejected.

swords-06.name: Six of Swords
swords-06.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A ferryman poles a boat across water, carrying two passengers: a woman with a child, huddled beneath a cloak. Six swords stand upright in the prow of the boat. They move from rough water toward calmer water.

swords-07.name: Seven of Swords
swords-07.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man tiptoes away from a camp, carrying five swords. He looks back over his shoulder with a sly expression. Two swords remain planted in the ground behind him. Tents and figures in the distance.

swords-08.name: Eight of Swords
swords-08.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A woman stands bound and blindfolded, surrounded by eight swords planted in the ground around her in a loose circle. She stands in a marsh near water. A castle appears in the background. She is trapped but the swords do not touch her.

swords-09.name: Nine of Swords
swords-09.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A figure sits up in bed, face buried in hands, in an attitude of despair. Nine swords hang horizontally on the wall behind them, all parallel. A patterned quilt covers the lower half of the figure. Night surrounds them.

swords-10.name: Ten of Swords
swords-10.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A figure lies face down on the ground with ten swords plunged into their back. The sky above is dark and stormy on the left but brightening on the horizon at right. The figure is still; the scene is one of complete defeat.

swords-knight.name: Knight of Swords
swords-knight.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A knight in full armor charges on a galloping horse, sword raised high and thrusting forward. The wind blows fiercely; clouds race and trees bend. His cloak flies behind him and the horse is in full gallop.

swords-queen.name: Queen of Swords
swords-queen.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A queen sits on a stone throne against a cloudy sky. She holds a long sword upright in her right hand and extends her left palm forward as if beckoning or receiving. A bird flies in the distance. Her expression is clear and precise.

swords-king.name: King of Swords
swords-king.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A king sits rigidly on a stone throne, holding an upright sword in his right hand. Clouds and wind surround him. He looks forward with a direct gaze. Butterflies are worked into his purple robe. His bearing is authoritative and impartial.

swords-page.name: Page of Swords
swords-page.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man strides across blustery ground, holding a sword raised high in both hands, its point tilted back. Clouds rush past and trees in the distance bend in the wind. He looks around alertly.

pentacles-ace.name: Ace of Pentacles
pentacles-ace.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A hand extends from a cloud holding a large golden pentacle. A garden path lined with flowers stretches beneath it, leading through an arch of roses into a landscape of mountains. White lilies bloom at the edges.

pentacles-02.name: Two of Pentacles
pentacles-02.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man balances two pentacles suspended in a figure-eight loop, juggling them dexterously. Ships ride enormous waves in the background. He dances lightly, managing the dynamic balance.

pentacles-03.name: Three of Pentacles
pentacles-03.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A sculptor or craftsman stands on a bench, working on the stonework above three arched windows in a cathedral. Two figures — a monk and a noblewoman — consult a plan or document and confer with him. The craftsman holds a chisel.

pentacles-04.name: Four of Pentacles
pentacles-04.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A crowned figure sits with arms wrapped tightly around a pentacle, one foot resting on a second pentacle, a third on his head, and a fourth on the ground beneath him. A city appears in the background. He clings to his wealth.

pentacles-05.name: Five of Pentacles
pentacles-05.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

Two ragged figures limp through snow past a stained-glass window glowing from inside a church. One walks on crutches; the other is bent and poorly dressed. The window above shows five pentacles arranged in a cross. They appear excluded from warmth and shelter.

pentacles-06.name: Six of Pentacles
pentacles-06.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A merchant holds scales in one hand while distributing coins to two kneeling beggars. Six pentacles are arranged overhead. The merchant appears to weigh and give with precision. The beggars receive humbly.

pentacles-07.name: Seven of Pentacles
pentacles-07.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A man leans on his hoe, pausing to look at seven pentacles growing from a vine-like plant before him. He appears to assess his harvest with a contemplative expression.

pentacles-08.name: Eight of Pentacles
pentacles-08.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A craftsman sits at a bench, carefully hammering pentacles into a staff or panel. Eight pentacles hang in a row to his left. He is absorbed in skilled, repetitive work. A town appears in the distant background.

pentacles-09.name: Nine of Pentacles
pentacles-09.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A woman stands in a vineyard, a falcon on her gloved hand. She is richly dressed and surrounded by ripening grapes and nine pentacles. A snail moves slowly near her foot.

pentacles-10.name: Ten of Pentacles
pentacles-10.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

An old man sits beneath an archway in a prosperous household. Two dogs rest beside him. A young couple and a child stand nearby. Ten pentacles are arranged in the Tree of Life pattern across the image. The scene suggests inherited wealth and family lineage.

pentacles-knight.name: Knight of Pentacles
pentacles-knight.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A knight in heavy black armor sits motionless on a large, still horse. He holds a pentacle before him, studying it. The landscape is a plowed field. His horse does not move. He is patient and methodical.

pentacles-queen.name: Queen of Pentacles
pentacles-queen.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A queen sits on a throne carved with goat heads, a pentacle in her lap. She gazes at it with maternal attentiveness. Flowers and fruit grow abundantly around her. A rabbit runs in the lower corner.

pentacles-king.name: King of Pentacles
pentacles-king.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A king sits on a throne decorated with bulls and vines. He rests his hand on a large pentacle on his knee. He wears a robe covered with grape clusters. A castle rises behind him and a bull's head appears on his crown.

pentacles-page.name: Page of Pentacles
pentacles-page.Scene:
*Editorial — The Recursive Tarot · what is pictured on this card*

A young man in a flower-bordered tunic stands in a meadow, holding a pentacle at eye level with both hands and gazing at it intently. Mountains and a forested landscape surround him. He appears absorbed in study or contemplation of the symbol.

emg-majors.name: The 22 Keys — The Paths of the Tree
emg-majors.Scene: The twenty-two major arcana of the Golden Dawn tradition are shown here with the Rider-Waite-Smith images that Arthur Edward Waite and Pamela Colman Smith created to embody the Golden Dawn teachings. Each image is a visual translation of esoteric symbolism intended to communicate meaning without verbal instruction.

emg-decans.name: The 36 Decans — Lords of the Minor Arcana
emg-decans.Scene: The thirty-six decans divide the zodiac wheel into ten-degree segments, each ruled by a planet according to the Chaldean system. In the Golden Dawn Book T system, each numbered pip card from Two through Ten corresponds to one decan. The RWS images for these cards were designed with the decan's planetary and zodiacal character in mind.

emg-suit-wands.name: Suit of Wands — Fire (Atziluth)
emg-suit-wands.Scene: The Wands suit in the Golden Dawn Book T system corresponds to the element of Fire and to the Yod (first letter) of the Tetragrammaton. The RWS images show scenes of action, ambition, conflict, and creative force consistent with the fiery nature of the suit.

emg-suit-cups.name: Suit of Cups — Water (Briah)
emg-suit-cups.Scene: The Cups suit corresponds to the element of Water and to the He (second letter) of the Tetragrammaton. The RWS images portray emotional, relational, and imaginative scenes — unions, dreams, grief, and contentment — all expressing the watery, receptive quality of this suit.

emg-suit-swords.name: Suit of Swords — Air (Yetzirah)
emg-suit-swords.Scene: The Swords suit corresponds to the element of Air and to the Vav (third letter) of the Tetragrammaton. The RWS images show scenes of conflict, loss, mental clarity, and severance, all expressing the sharp, discriminating nature of air as force of mind.

emg-suit-pentacles.name: Suit of Pentacles — Earth (Assiah)
emg-suit-pentacles.Scene: The Pentacles suit corresponds to the element of Earth and to the final He of the Tetragrammaton. The RWS images portray material life — work, wealth, nature, and the body — grounded in earthly experience and the physical world.

kw-minor-arcana.name: Minor arcana
kw-minor-arcana.Scene: The fifty-six minor arcana of the Book T system encode the full range of human experience across four elements and a hierarchy of social roles. The pip cards map the arc of each element from pure potential (Ace) through culmination (Ten); the court cards embody the social and elemental personalities that inhabit each suit.

kw-decan.name: Decan
kw-decan.Scene: The thirty-six decan attributions connect each numbered pip card to a ten-degree segment of the zodiac and a planetary ruler. In the Book T system, the image and meaning of each pip card encode both the element of its suit and the specific quality of the decan it governs.

kw-major-arcana.name: Major arcana
kw-major-arcana.Scene: The twenty-two major arcana in the Golden Dawn system correspond to the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the twenty-two paths of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life. The RWS images were designed to encode these correspondences in visual form accessible to initiates and students alike.

kw-court-card.name: Court card
kw-court-card.Scene: The sixteen court cards in the Book T system represent elemental sub-types within each suit. The Page (Princess), Knight (Prince), Queen, and King of each suit blend the suit's primary element with a secondary elemental quality, producing a matrix of sixteen elemental personalities.

kw-air.name: Air
kw-air.Scene: Air is the element of the Swords suit in the Book T system. It governs intellect, communication, conflict, and the discriminating power of mind. The Hebrew letter Vav (and the Ruach, or intellect, of the soul) are associated with this element in Golden Dawn teaching.

kw-water.name: Water
kw-water.Scene: Water is the element of the Cups suit in the Book T system. It governs feeling, imagination, and the unconscious. In the Golden Dawn schema water corresponds to the He of the Tetragrammaton and to the emotional capacity of the soul.

kw-cups.name: Cups
kw-cups.Scene: The Cups suit governs the realm of emotional life, dreams, and relationships. In Book T teaching, cups are associated with water and the He of YHVH. RWS images in this suit tend toward interior scenes of feeling and connection.

kw-earth.name: Earth
kw-earth.Scene: Earth is the element of the Pentacles suit. It governs the physical world, material resources, practical skill, and the body. In Golden Dawn teaching earth corresponds to the final He of the Tetragrammaton and to the Assiah (physical) world.

kw-fire.name: Fire
kw-fire.Scene: Fire is the element of the Wands suit. It governs will, creativity, ambition, and the life force. In Golden Dawn teaching fire corresponds to the Yod of the Tetragrammaton and to the divine creative impulse.

kw-pentacles.name: Pentacles
kw-pentacles.Scene: The Pentacles suit governs the material world — resources, craft, skill, nature, and the body. In Book T the pentacle is the Earth symbol of the four tools of magic, corresponding to the physical plane (Assiah) and the final He of YHVH.

kw-swords.name: Swords
kw-swords.Scene: The Swords suit governs the life of the mind and social conflict. In Book T, swords correspond to Air and Vav, the connecting principle of the Tetragrammaton. RWS Swords images are often scenes of difficulty, clarity, or decisive action.

kw-wands.name: Wands
kw-wands.Scene: The Wands suit governs will, ambition, and creative action. In Book T, wands correspond to Fire and Yod, the initial divine impulse. RWS Wands images show figures in motion, striving, competing, or leading.

kw-knight.name: Knight
kw-knight.Scene: In the Book T system the Knight corresponds to what later decks call the King — the most active and mobile expression of the court. Each Knight combines the element of his suit with the sub-element of Fire, producing a fiery, initiating version of that element.

kw-queen.name: Queen
kw-queen.Scene: The Queen embodies the watery, receptive aspect of each suit element. In the Book T system the Queen is associated with the He of the Tetragrammaton at the elemental level — she receives and nurtures the creative impulse of the Knight.

kw-ace.name: Ace
kw-ace.Scene: The Ace of each suit in the Book T system represents the Root of its element in its purest, most undivided form. The Ace is the first emanation of the Sephirah Kether into each of the four elemental worlds.

kw-king.name: King
kw-king.Scene: In the original Book T system what later decks label King is the Knight — the most active court figure. In adapted Golden Dawn decks the King sits at the pinnacle of the court hierarchy, expressing the solar, authority-bearing aspect of each element.

kw-page.name: Page
kw-page.Scene: The Page (or Princess in Book T terminology) represents the earthly expression of each suit element — the grounded, practical, receptive level at which the element manifests in daily life.

kw-prince.name: Prince
kw-prince.Scene: The Prince corresponds to what Waite calls the Knight — the airy, intellectual, mobile aspect of each suit element. In the Book T system the Prince (son of the Knight and Queen) traverses the element with speed and mental agility.

kw-princess.name: Princess
kw-princess.Scene: The Princess is the earthly daughter-figure in the Book T court system. She represents the element in its most material and practical form, closest to the physical world and farthest from its original divine fire.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: Browse the Golden Dawn Book T tarot by keyword — suit, element, number, court rank, decan attribution, and thematic grouping.
